title: Coefficient-tower coherence of the specified quotient-completion exchange
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $R\xrightarrow a S\xrightarrow b V$ be homomorphisms of sheaves of commutative rings. Assume $S$ is finite free as an $R$-module sheaf and $V$ finite free as an $S$-module sheaf (ranks may be zero). Let $t\in R(1)$, $v\in S(1)$ and $w\in V(1)$ act injectively on their respective rings, with $a(t)=u v^e$ and $b(v)=z w^f$, where $u,z$ are units and $e,f\geq1$. Assume countable products of $R$-, $S$-, $V$-modules and of abelian sheaves are exact. Use the unbounded derived module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the derived scalar functors $T_a=-\otimes_R^L S$, $T_b=-\otimes_S^L V$, $T_{ba}=-\otimes_R^L V$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and the balanced scalar associator $\alpha:T_bT_a\xrightarrow\sim T_{ba}$, induced by $((p\otimes s)\otimes q)\mapsto p\otimes b(s)q$. For $A=R,S,V$ and $h=t,v,w$ respectively put
$$C_AQ=R\lim_{n\geq1}(Q\otimes_A^L A/h^nA),$$
using the strict quotient tower and its quotient augmentation $\eta^A$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. For each of $a,b,ba$, let $\epsilon$ be precisely the exchange isomorphism of [lem-pur-finite-free-completion-exchange]: the canonical tensor/product map, followed by quotient tensor associativity and the inverse of the selected-coordinate/weighted-block arithmetic-subsequence Roos map of [lem-pur-compact-support-roos-cofinality]. For $ba$ use exponent $ef$, since $(ba)(t)=b(u)z^e w^{ef}$.
Then for every $Q\in D(R)$ the following equality holds in $D(V)$, naturally in $Q$:
$$C_V(\alpha_Q)\circ\epsilon^b_{T_aQ}\circ T_b(\epsilon^a_Q)=\epsilon^{ba}_Q\circ\alpha_{C_RQ}.$$
Thus both routes from $T_bT_aC_RQ$ to $C_VT_{ba}Q$ agree for the specified maps, including their quotient augmentations. For the identity map of any one of these ring sheaves, with the same chosen section and exponent $1$, the exchange is the identity on $C_AQ$ under the scalar multiplication identification $Q\otimes_A^LA\cong Q$. After composing with the specified arithmetic restriction quasi-isomorphisms, the tower equation is represented by equality of the actual maps on both Roos product coordinates. The displayed equality therefore also holds under the normalized strict-derived-limit comparisons [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison]. No completeness, constructibility, boundedness or perfectness hypothesis on $Q$ is imposed.

proof.text: Choose a K-flat resolution $P\to Q$ with flat terms. Write $E_a=-\otimes_R S$, $E_b=-\otimes_S V$, $E_{ba}=-\otimes_R V$ on complexes. The cited derived-change-of-rings theorem computes $T_aQ$ by $E_aP$ and $T_{ba}Q$ by $E_{ba}P$. These are K-flat over the new rings: for an acyclic $S$-complex $N$, restriction to $R$ is acyclic and $N\otimes_S E_aP\cong(\operatorname{Res}_R N)\otimes_R P$ is acyclic by the definition of K-flatness; the same argument applies to $b$ and $ba$. Thus $T_bT_aQ$ is represented by $E_bE_aP$, and its specified associator is the chain isomorphism $((p\otimes s)\otimes q)\mapsto p\otimes b(s)q$. The inverse sends $p\otimes q$ to $(p\otimes1)\otimes q$. These balanced formulas commute with differentials since scalars have degree zero.

proof.text: If $S$ has $R$-basis $(s_i)_{i<d}$, then the underlying $R$-module functor $E_a$ is $M\mapsto M^{\oplus d}$. It is exact, hence preserves acyclic complexes and quasi-isomorphisms, so it computes $T_a$ on every complex, including a Roos complex which need not be K-flat. Its canonical product comparison is invertible: a family of $d$-tuples is sent back to the $d$-tuple of families. This is the inverse of the map with $n$-th projection $E_a(\mathrm{pr}_n)$. The argument also applies to $b$. A basis of $V$ over $S$ and one of $S$ over $R$ give the $R$-basis $(s_iq_j)_{i,j}$ of $V$, so it applies to $ba$. Empty bases give the zero functor. The coordinate maps themselves use only projections, and therefore are independent of all these bases.

proof.text: Put $X_n=P\otimes_R R/t^n$, $Y_m=E_aP\otimes_S S/v^m$, $Z_k=E_{ba}P\otimes_V V/w^k$, all with quotient transitions, for indices at least $1$. Write $H$ for the actual shifted Roos cone. For a tower $K$ let $K^{(d)}_n=K_{dn}$. The exchange statement supplies canonical chain isomorphisms $\Theta_a:E_aH(X)\to H(Y^{(e)})$, $\Theta_b:E_bH(Y)\to H(Z^{(f)})$, and $\Theta_{ba}:E_{ba}H(X)\to H(Z^{(ef)})$, before the arithmetic restriction is inverted. We have used the chain associator of Step 1 to identify the $b$-target tower with $Z^{(f)}$. Let $\Theta_b^{(e)}:E_bH(Y^{(e)})\to H((Z^{(f)})^{(e)})=H(Z^{(ef)})$ be the same tensor/product and quotient maps on the restricted tower. Write $r_d(K):H(K)\to H(K^{(d)})$ for the specified restriction. In the derived category the stipulated exchanges are exactly $\epsilon^a=r_e(Y)^{-1}\Theta_a$, $\epsilon^b=r_f(Z)^{-1}\Theta_b$, and $\epsilon^{ba}=r_{ef}(Z)^{-1}\Theta_{ba}$. Their isomorphism assertions apply: $V$ is finite free over $R$ by Step 2 and $(ba)(t)=b(u)z^e w^{ef}$ with unit $b(u)z^e$ and $ef\ge1$.

proof.text: Check the quotient identifications without introducing a unit multiplier into the maps. Since $a(t^n)=u^nv^{en}$, the ideals generated by these two sections agree. The map $(R/t^n)\otimes_R S\to S/v^{en}$ sends $\bar r\otimes s$ to $\overline{a(r)s}$; its inverse sends $\bar s$ to $\bar1\otimes s$. Likewise $b(v^m)=z^mw^{fm}$. For the composite, both quotient routes send $((\bar r\otimes s)\otimes q)$ to $\overline{(ba)(r)b(s)q}$ modulo $w^{efn}$. The formulas respect quotient transitions because reducing a representative before or after multiplication gives the same residue. Tensoring with $P$ gives strictly commuting tower identifications. These are maps of sheaves: the formulas are balanced on presheaves and extend to the defining sheafified tensors. Units change the ideals, never the residue-class formula.

proof.text:
The tensor/product comparisons compose with scalar reassociation on both product coordinates. Indeed, for any family $(M_n)$, project the two maps from $E_bE_a(\prod_n M_n)$ to $\prod_n E_{ba}M_n$ to the $n$-th factor. Both are $\alpha_{M_n}E_bE_a(\mathrm{pr}_n)$, by naturality of the balanced formula of Step 1; on local tensor generators they send $((x\otimes s)\otimes q)$ to $\mathrm{pr}_n(x)\otimes b(s)q$. The product universal property gives equality. Combining this with Step 4 on the two diagonal coordinates of the cone gives the actual chain-map equation
$$\Theta_b^{(e)} E_b(\Theta_a)=\Theta_{ba}\alpha_{H(X)}.$$
There is no unspecified cone isomorphism here: the coordinate formula for $H$ has differential $(y,x)\mapsto(-dy-(1-s)x,dx)$, and the two maps just checked are its two diagonal components.

proof.text:
The additive Roos comparison applies to $E_b$ by the canonical product invertibility of Step 2. Its arithmetic compatibility, followed by the quotient identifications of Step 4, gives
$$r_e(Z^{(f)})\Theta_b=\Theta_b^{(e)}E_b(r_e(Y)).$$
Here these are actual chain maps over the possibly nonconstant ring sheaves. Explicitly, selection at $en$ commutes with $E_b(\mathrm{pr}_{en})$. For the other coordinate, writing $Y_{j,i}$ for the transition $Y_i\to Y_j$, the projection is $\sum_{i=en}^{e(n+1)-1}Y_{en,i}\mathrm{pr}_i$; the additive functor carries this finite sum to the corresponding sum for $Z^{(f)}$. Quotient naturality identifies $E_b(Y_{en,i})$ with $Z_{fen,fi}$. Thus the cited additive statement has exactly the two required coordinates; no constant-ring cofinality theorem is applied to a nonconstant sheaf.

proof.text:
For completeness check the order of arithmetic composition directly in the category of $V$-modules. For any tower $K$ write $K_{j,i}$ for its transition from $i$ to $j$. The selected coordinate of $r_e(K^{(f)})r_f(K)$ is $x_{fen}$. The weighted coordinate is
$$\sum_{j=en}^{e(n+1)-1}K_{fen,fj}\sum_{i=fj}^{f(j+1)-1}K_{fj,i}y_i
=\sum_{i=efn}^{ef(n+1)-1}K_{efn,i}y_i.$$
Indeed $K_{fen,fj}K_{fj,i}=K_{fen,i}$, and the $e$ adjacent blocks of length $f$ partition exactly the displayed interval. Both coordinates therefore equal those of $r_{ef}(K)$, proving the strict equation $r_e(K^{(f)})r_f(K)=r_{ef}(K)$. When $d=1$, selection is identity and each weighted sum has its single identity-transition term, hence $r_1(K)=1$. These finite identities also prove the chain-map square, since the block sum of $(1-s)y$ telescopes to $y_{dn}-K_{dn,d(n+1)}y_{d(n+1)}$.

proof.text:
Pass the chain equations to the derived category. In the identifications of Step 3, multiply the desired two-stage map by $r_{ef}(Z)$ on the left. Steps 6 and 7 give, with composition read right to left,
$$\begin{aligned}
r_{ef}(Z)\epsilon^b E_b(\epsilon^a)
&=r_e(Z^{(f)})\Theta_b E_b(\epsilon^a)\\
&=\Theta_b^{(e)}E_b(r_e(Y)\epsilon^a)\\
&=\Theta_b^{(e)}E_b(\Theta_a)
=\Theta_{ba}\alpha_{H(X)}.
\end{aligned}$$
Also $r_{ef}(Z)\epsilon^{ba}\alpha_{H(X)}=\Theta_{ba}\alpha_{H(X)}$. The specified $r_{ef}(Z)$ is invertible by the exchange construction for $ba$, so cancellation proves equality. Restoring the chain associator on the output tower restores exactly the factor $C_V(\alpha_Q)$ in the question. Every equality before this cancellation was equality of both actual product coordinates after the specified arithmetic maps, rather than uniqueness of a map of distinguished triangles.

proof.text: The quotient augmentation has coordinates $(0,(P\to P/h^n)_n)$. A tensor/product comparison carries it to the scalar-extended quotient family. Selection carries that family to its subsequence and the weighted coordinate sends zero to zero. Thus the preceding equations preserve these augmentations, as also asserted for each $\epsilon$ by the exchange theorem. For an identity coefficient map with the same section and exponent $1$, multiplication $p\otimes a\mapsto ap$ identifies the tensor/product map and each quotient map with identity; Step 7 gives $r_1=1$. Hence the specified exchange is identity. All displayed formulas commute with chain maps in $P$. The exchange theorem already states naturality on $D(R)$, so the equality is natural in $Q$, independently of the resolution chosen in Step 1.

proof.text: Finally use the natural normalized comparison $\rho_K:H(K)\xrightarrow\sim R\lim K$ for ring-sheaf modules with exact countable products. Its stated normalization is $H(K)\to H(I)\leftarrow\lim I$, where the right arrow has coordinates $(0,(\mathrm{pr}_n)_n)$, and it sends strict quotient augmentations to the canonical derived augmentations. Replace each Roos vertex of the equality of Step 8 by its image under this same $\rho$. The two occurrences of each intermediate $\rho$ and its inverse cancel; naturality identifies the final reassociation with $C_V(\alpha_Q)$. This is precisely the equality under the normalized strict-derived-limit comparisons. Their hypotheses hold for each of $R,S,V$ by assumption. No step imposed a bound on $P$, and no step used completeness, constructibility or perfectness.
